text.title: Growth Loops Output Contract
text.summary: JSON Schema (draft-07) for the growth-loop spec: four named stages closed by a tracked fuel-back event in the same unit as the input, exactly one primary loop type with its input source, a stage-metrics table where every transition is measured (event, numerator, denominator, date, sample) or flagged as an assumption, loop efficiency k as the product of the stages with cycle time and the amplifier reading below 1, a cohort projection over at least 90 days and three cycles with a decay term, a friction map naming the lowest stage as the bottleneck with experiments ranked on it, CAC payback with and without loop-sourced users attributed by the fuel-back event, and a numeric quality guardrail. Validator at scripts/validate-growth-loops.py enforces it, including the k product, the bottleneck choice and the cohort arithmetic.

required.field: short name of the loop being specified
exactly one of viral, ugc_search, paid, network_effect, supply_side (r-one-primary-loop-type)
what the loop type consumes: user_action, content, capital or supply (r-one-primary-loop-type)
other loops present, each `type` and `note`; may be empty; never summed into the projection (r-one-primary-loop-type)

three transitions (input-action, action-output, output-fuel_back) each with `event`, `numerator`, `denominator`, `value`, `basis` measured or assumption; measured rows carry `measured_on` and `sample_size` (r-stage-conversion-measured-not-estimated)

`k` = product of the stage values, `cycle_time_days` median input to fuel-back, `reading` amplifier (k below 1, with `multiplier` 1 / (1 - k)) or self_sustaining (k at or above 1, with `growth_rate_per_cycle` = k - 1) (r-loop-efficiency-and-cycle-time)

`horizon_days` at least 90 and at least three cycle times, `cycles` at least 3, `decay` with `kind` and `rate_per_cycle`, `rests_on_assumption`, `headline`, and `cohorts[]` built cycle by cycle with `external_inputs`, `loop_inputs`, `total_inputs` (r-steady-state-projection-90-days)

`bottleneck_stage` = the transition with the lowest value, `bottleneck_value`, `k_if_doubled`, and `experiments[]` ranked with the bottleneck first; a non-bottleneck experiment carries `justification` (r-friction-map-names-the-bottleneck)
`period_days`, `attributed_by` (the fuel-back event), `without_loop` and `with_loop` each with `blended_cac` and `payback_months` (r-cac-payback-with-and-without-loop)
`metric` (activation_rate, d30_retention or indexed_and_trafficked_share), `threshold`, `loop_cohort_value`, `baseline_value`, `status` within or breached (r-loop-quality-guardrail)

forbidden.pattern: `loop_type` naming two types ("viral and content"), or a secondary loop's inputs added to `projection.cohorts[]` — r-one-primary-loop-type

a stage metric with `basis` other than measured or assumption, or a measured row without `measured_on` and `sample_size`, or `rests_on_assumption` false while a stage is an assumption — assumed-stage-rate-as-measured
`efficiency.k` not equal to the product of the stage values, or `reading` self_sustaining with k below 1, or `multiplier` not 1 / (1 - k) — k-below-one-called-viral
`projection.horizon_days` below 90, `cycles` below 3, no `decay`, or a cohort whose `loop_inputs` exceed the previous cohort's total times k — first-cycle-linear-extrapolation
`friction_map.bottleneck_stage` not the lowest-value transition, or the rank-1 experiment on another stage, or a non-bottleneck experiment with no `justification` — optimising-the-owned-stage
`cac_payback.attributed_by` other than the fuel-back event (organic, direct, "loop" as a channel label) — r-cac-payback-with-and-without-loop
`quality_guardrail.status` within while `loop_cohort_value` is below `threshold`, or a guardrail with no numeric threshold — loop-optimised-into-spam

list.item: `stages.fuel_back.event` is a tracked event and its unit is the input unit; if it is not, the design is a funnel and the projection stops.
`efficiency.k` equals the product of the three stage values to two decimals; below 1 the reading is amplifier with multiplier 1 / (1 - k).
`projection.horizon_days` covers at least 90 days and three cycle times; every cohort's `loop_inputs` is at most the previous total times k, and `total_inputs` = `external_inputs` + `loop_inputs`.
`friction_map.bottleneck_stage` is the transition with the lowest value and the rank-1 experiment targets it.

text.reference: Validator implementing this schema and the cross-field rules (unit closure, k product and multiplier, projection span and cohort arithmetic, bottleneck choice, attribution event, guardrail status).
